`bindaxis <physical axis>` without a virtual axis leaves the axis at GPAD_VIRTAXIS_NONE (-1) and still stores the binding at gaGlobs[0].virtualAxes[-1], which is axesValues[4..5] (the trigger values) instead of rejecting the command.

description: A one-character key name returns the char as a signed value, so a byte >= 0x80 gives keynum -128..-1. Key_Bind_f, Key_Unbind_f and Key_SwapBind_f then write keys[keynum].binding up to 1.5 KB before playerKeys (chat field, then gaGlobs, the Axis_*_f_VAR command nodes with their function pointers, cl_input's dvar pointers, playersKb); Key_IsDown/Key_GetBinding read there. `unbind \x80` overwrites the low half of a pointer with 0.
evidence: reproduced by tests/differential/test_input.py (bind/unbind/bind_swap with "\x80", "\xe9", "\xff": the original writes playerKeys-0x4D4 and playerKeys+0x18); reachable from the console and config files; whether a server can make a client run bind/unbind still needs checking (docs/security.md)

description: The mouse is read as the system cursor's movement (GetCursorPos minus the last position, then SetCursorPos back to the window centre), not as raw device counts, so Windows' pointer speed and "Enhance pointer precision" acceleration are applied to aim, and the movement is sampled once per client frame.
evidence: src/win32/win_input.cpp IN_MouseMove reproduces it (tests/differential/test_win_input.py, IN_Frame, 1500 cases); every frame with the game window in front

description: In fullscreen (r_displayMode 0) the cursor is clamped to the window rectangle before the movement is measured, so one frame can't register more than the distance from the centre to the window edge (about 960 counts horizontally at 1920x1080); a fast flick at a low frame rate loses the rest.
evidence: reproduced by tests/differential/test_win_input.py (cursor positions on and beyond the window edges); fullscreen only

description: Every unacknowledged reliable command (up to 128, each up to 1023 characters) is written into a 2048-byte message without checking msg.overflowed. The MSG writers stop at maxsize and set the flag, so the "Overflow compressed msg buf" check never fires and the client sends a truncated packet without its usercmds and end marker.
evidence: tests/differential/test_cl_input_sendcmd.py (message sizes at the 0x800 boundary); reachable by queuing many long reliable commands while the server isn't acknowledging

description: At most 32 usercmds go into a packet; older ones are dropped silently (Black Ops printed MAX_PACKET_USERCMDS).
evidence: reconstruction (count capped at 32); at low packet rates with high frame rates

description: Packets are rate-limited by integer 1000 / cl_maxpackets with cl_maxpackets at most 100, so above 100 fps commands are batched; only loopback is exempt (LAN servers are limited too).
The spawn-sight masks are built with 1 << i for a 16-bit point count into 32-bit masks; points 32 and up (the array holds about 75) shift past the width and set wrong bits.

Remote-control steering with the mouse uses each frame's mouse movement times m_yaw/m_pitch directly as stick deflection (clamped to +-1 per frame), so the same hand movement steers less at higher frame rates.
evidence: reconstruction (tests/differential/test_cl_input_createcmd.py); every remote-controlled vehicle/killstreak with a mouse

description: The location-selection aspect ratio divides by compassMapWorldSize[1]; a zero gives inf/NaN, the clamps let NaN through and it is sent as selectedLoc 0.
evidence: reconstruction; only with bad map compass data

description: While eFlags 0x200000 is set, both the left trigger and GPAD_B set button bit 0x2000000; probably a copy-paste error (could be intended, to check in game).
The analog attack threshold is hard-coded at 0.8 (Black Ops had cl_analog_attack_threshold).
The stance-key hold times are hard-coded (200 ms sprinting, 300 ms otherwise; Black Ops read cl_dtpHoldTime/cl_stanceHoldTime).

With r_aspectRatio "auto" the window's shape is rounded to one of three: n = floor(16*h/w + 0.5) is 10 → 16:10, below 10 → 16:9, above → 4:3. Every ultrawide (21:9, 32:9) is treated as 16:9, so the projection's aspect (cgs.viewAspect) doesn't match the viewport and the picture is stretched sideways; 5:4 is treated as 4:3. There is no way to give the real ratio.
evidence: Store disassembly (140630670); the aspect goes to cls.vidConfig.windowAspectRatio and cgs.viewAspect, which CG_CalcFov multiplies into tanHalfFovX

description: cg_fov is registered with the range 65-80, the horizontal FOV at 4:3 (80.7°-96.4° horizontal at 16:9; MW2019 allows 60-120).

The mouse sensitivity scale is tan(fov/2)/tan(32.5°), relative to the fixed default 65 rather than to the player's cg_fov, and it applies to hip fire as well (CL_SetFOVSensitivityScale in 1402AB060). Raising cg_fov raises hip-fire sensitivity: ×1.317 at cg_fov 80.
evidence: reconstruction (src/cgame/cg_camera.cpp, tests/differential/test_cg_camera.py); 1402AB060 passes zoomSensitivity to CL_SetFOVSensitivityScale (140306E80, clientActive_t::cgameFOVSensitivityScale)

description: com_maxfps defaults to 85 and its maximum is 100.

The SOCKS5 username/password request is built in a 64-byte stack buffer with the full lengths of net_socksUsername and net_socksPassword and no bound; more than 61 bytes together overwrite the saved registers and the return address (no stack cookie). The length bytes in the request are truncated to 8 bits.
evidence: Store disassembly 14054F74D-14054F788 (buffer at [RBP-0x40]); reconstruction src/win32/win_net.cpp, tests/differential/test_win_net.py

description: A 2- or 3-byte UDP ASSOCIATE reply is accepted; the relay address is then taken from the request still in the buffer (0.0.0.0 and our own port). The reply length isn't checked against 10.

The packet length is never checked against the 1280-byte stack buffer: the checksum copy and the two checksum bytes at buf[length] run past it for length > 1278 (no stack cookie). Whether every caller bounds the length is not established; the caller's loopback copy into 0x4F8-byte slots doesn't check either.
A 0- or 1-byte datagram makes it read the checksum from before the buffer (data[-2], data[-1]); any host can send one.
Sys_StringToAdr and Sys_StringToSockaddr pick an address with I_irand(0, count); for a host with no addresses that dereferences h_addr_list[0], a null pointer.

Sockets leak: NET_IPSocket keeps the socket when ioctlsocket or setsockopt fails, and NET_OpenSocks leaves its TCP socket open on every error path (only NET_Config closes it). Sys_GetLocalIP doesn't check its index against the number of addresses.

LUI's Lua keeps package.loadlib and require's C-module loader: a script can LoadLibraryA any DLL and call its functions (1401C6710, 1401DAA90). Only the fastfile signature check stands between a script and native code.
evidence: Store pseudocode: luaopen_package registers "loadlib" (14010000.c:83416); LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress in 1401C6710 and 1401DAA90

description: Load_Texture (and the streaming upload 14062B580) lay out faces x mips subresource entries in a fixed 4096-entry stack array with no bound: a texture asset with a large numElements x levelCount overflows the stack.

The streaming upload passes Image_CountMipmaps(level size) entries to UpdateSubresource but only fills the level's levelCount entries; when they differ (or levelCount is 0) uninitialised entries reach the driver.
A map type outside 3-6 (including 1D) falls through to cube creation, which reads five faces of entries that were never filled.
With the multisample flag, a render target missing from the 12-entry multisample table (1408A9070) is looked up as NULL and dereferenced.

The mode count from GetDisplayModeList is used as the capacity of dx.displayModes[256] (and two 257-entry stack lists) with no check, so a system reporting more than 256 R8G8B8A8 modes overflows into the following DxGlobals fields.
A display mode whose RefreshRate.Denominator is 0 divides by zero.

Neither D3D11CreateDevice nor CreateSwapChain is checked; R_CreateDevice always returns true and the game crashes later without a device. Most other creation calls (textures, views, constant buffers) are unchecked too, and R_CreateDepthStencilSurface / R_InitPIPRenderTargets then Release NULL.

MakeWindowAssociation(NO_WINDOW_CHANGES) is given dx.windows[0].hwnd, which is still NULL at first creation, so DXGI's Alt+Enter handling is only blocked after a device reset. The adapter's wide Description is printed with %s (first character only).
FormatMessageA's output pointer is not initialised before the call; error texts built with va() for Sys_DirectXFatalError are discarded (it takes no message).
The catch-up loop runs about 2^32 times if g_gpuSwapFrame is ahead of g_gpuSubmitSwapFrame.
GPU waits are GetData spin loops with no timeout: 14067D210 polls while holding the immediate-context lock, 14068BE20 stalls the render thread with Sleep(0), 14062DFF0 and R_FinishGpuFence likewise.
The occlusion update loops forever once the frame counter goes negative (after 2^31 frames), and with MSAA and multiSampleType 0 it divides 0/0.

Writes through whatever the buffer allocators return, NULL when r_loadForRenderer is off or Map fails; R_AllocStaticIndexBuffer/VertexBuffer Map even after a failed CreateBuffer and leave *ib dangling after a failed Map; R_GetConstantBufferHandleOfSize loops forever for a zone with more than 255 constant buffers and no size match.

The blend-op table has 6 entries but is indexed with & 7 (ops 6-7 read the next table); 140630A70 writes past its stack description for more than 8 render targets (callers pass 1); R_SetWndParms' r_aaMode switch has no range check.
The swap fences (g_gpuSwapFence) are written every present but never read: the engine never limits how far the GPU falls behind, leaving it to DXGI's default queue of 3 frames.
Keys and buttons are read by the message pump at the start of the frame, before the com_maxfps wait and the GPU sync, so they are older than the mouse movement read later in CL_Input.
The frame pacing term in R_SyncGpu is capped at 12 ms (an assumption of about 83 Hz).
R_PopRemoteScreenUpdate spins forever when called off the main thread while the nesting count is non-zero.
Writes the lifetime at addressHandles[unsigned index] without validating the index; only the reserved local index is skipped. Invalid indices can write outside the table.
evidence: Store disassembly 1405A9E50-1405A9E96 and tests/differential/test_dwnet.py preserve the unchecked write. Caller 1404D86A0 passes several stored addresses; ability of a current caller to supply an invalid index is not established.

description: A positive one-byte receive result with a nonnull handle is decremented by two and sign-extended to a 64-bit memmove length, producing an enormous copy instead of rejecting a short transport envelope.
evidence: Store disassembly/pseudocode at 1405A9740; src/dw/dwnet.cpp preserves result -= 2 before memmove. Current router reaching this state from an actual peer has not been established; SDK results are modeled in differential tests.

evidence: Store disassembly 1405A87E0-1405A8826; test_dwlifetime.py preserves writes including indices beyond the active range within mapped table storage. Reachability of an invalid index from a current caller is not established.

description: Linking enhanced vendor guards into recon.dll does not redirect calls that still enter their original executable addresses; the original telemetry sender can still reach its vendor lobby and SDK path.
evidence: Original internal calls target the EXE entry rather than DLL exports. tests/offline/run.py validates 31 explicit entry redirects and an unchanged original account thunk in a packaged image. Fixed only for the P0011 startup package and reviewed entries; native launch and other original vendor paths remain unverified.

description: PmoveSingle rounds the velocity to whole units per second at the end of every movement step, and Pmove takes one step per usercmd, so jump height, jump distance, acceleration and stopping distance depend on the command length, i.e. the client's frame rate: jump peak 31.3 units at 2 ms or shorter commands, 36.5 at 7 ms, 39.06 at 5 and 10 ms, 41.3 at 8 ms, 46.4 at 3 ms. The server runs Pmove on the same commands, so it agrees: the advantage is real online.
evidence: docs/fps.md; measured with the Store build's Pmove (140273A90) in the emulator

description: Pmove simulates one PmoveSingle per command (splitting only above 66 ms), with no fixed-step option: the root of the frame-rate dependent movement (the velocity rounding in Sys_SnapVector).
At 500-1000 fps a usercmd can get the same serverTime as the previous one when the client's time offset is nudged down by 1 ms; the server ignores a command that isn't newer, and its input is lost.
A packet carries at most 32 usercmds: above about 960 fps commands are lost between packets, and above about 480 fps the duplicates that protect against packet loss no longer fit.
Prediction replays every unacknowledged usercmd each frame from a 128-command ring: at 1000 fps that covers only 128 ms of latency, and the work per second grows with fps squared times the ping.
enhanced: fixed: P0016 (5 ms commands bound the replay window to 640 ms)

description: The packet send interval is rounded up to whole frames, so packets per second depend on the frame rate (20.8 at 62.5 fps vs 30.3 at 333 fps and above with cl_maxpackets 30).

The view kick integrates in steps of up to 5 ms of the integer cg.frametime, so it matches only at frame times that are multiples of 5 ms: at 1000 fps the kick peaks about 7% lower and recovers sooner. The kicked angles go into the usercmd, so the server sees the difference.
evidence: docs/fps-frame.md; measured with the Store function in the emulator

description: The viewmodel recoil integrates in steps of up to 5 ms of the frame time: its peak is 12% lower at 1 ms frames and it settles anywhere from 120 to 170 ms.

The client's time base is whole milliseconds with 1 ms corrections, so at frame periods that aren't whole milliseconds (240 Hz, 400 fps) frame interpolation advances unevenly (+20% every sixth frame at 240 Hz): other players, effects and the camera's translation move unevenly.
The radar jamming level moves 1/15 of the way to its target per frame: 250 ms to settle at 60 fps, 15 ms at 1000 fps.
Doppler pitch smoothing (snd_dopplerSmoothing) is a weight per sound update, which runs once or more per frame, so it smooths less as the frame rate rises.

Normal NA_IP game traffic is sent through dwSendTo and receive falls back to dwRecvFrom; disabling vendor services therefore also disables direct game traffic. Original address comparisons use DW handles rather than IP endpoints.
evidence: tests/direct/transport.py proves actual independent UDP exchange; tests/direct/game.py runs the original challenge resend through the packaged replacements. P0012 applies only to the explicit direct profile; server admission and native gameplay remain pending.

description: Raw UDP alone does not admit a player: retail direct-connect admission still expects an existing registered party/session slot, account identity and matching stats/session data. The terminal online branch returns EXE_ERR_UNREGISTERED_CONNECTION. P0012 selects onlinegame=false and tests/direct/admission.py exercises that local-network admission branch through its response boundary with game VM/response callbacks modeled. Map startup, identity/profile/stats lifecycle and real gameplay remain unverified.
evidence: Store pseudocode/disassembly 1404BC1D0-1404BCD0B, especially party lookup 1404D8440 and the final rejection. Client 140311570 still builds xuid/xnaddr and stats fields; connectResponse parser 1403129D0 uses session data helpers. Native launch/map admission not yet reproduced.

description: When no command is newer than the predicted state, the last frame's view angles are put back, so the view doesn't turn on frames with a repeated cl.serverTime (at 500 fps and above); with fixed-length commands it would be most frames.
The prediction error decay drops the whole error when its fraction reaches 1, so an error found in a frame whose cg.time didn't advance snaps instead of decaying.

On or within a second of an entity or moving platform, the predicted state is reset from the snapshot every frame, so the whole unacknowledged window of commands is replayed every frame (with 5 ms commands, about 25 replays a frame).
